subject: psychiatry
title: Cannabis, stimulants, nicotine and other substances

steps.tx: Heavy **cannabis** use produces craving, tolerance and a recognisable withdrawal syndrome after cessation in regular users. Withdrawal includes irritability, insomnia, vivid dreams and appetite loss and peaks several days after stopping. Intoxication impairs driving ability and learning because attention and short term memory suffer noticeably. Daily high potency use during adolescence increases **psychosis risk** and can precipitate schizophrenia in vulnerable young people. **Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome** causes repeated vomiting that hot bathing relieves temporarily until cessation occurs.
steps.say: Heavy cannabis use produces craving, tolerance and withdrawal after regular users stop. Withdrawal includes irritability, insomnia, vivid dreams and reduced appetite for several days. Intoxication impairs driving and learning because attention and memory suffer quite noticeably. Daily high potency adolescent use increases psychosis risk in vulnerable young people considerably.

steps.tx: Drugs such as cocaine and amphetamines are **stimulants** that produce euphoria, mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension and hyperthermia during intoxication. Severe toxicity causes chest pain, arrhythmia, seizures, rhabdomyolysis and excited delirium in affected patients. **Benzodiazepines** are first line treatment because they reduce agitation and the cardiovascular surge safely. Withdrawal produces hypersomnia, increased appetite and dysphoria with an important risk of suicide. **Contingency management** has the best evidence because no approved substitution medicine exists for stimulant dependence.
steps.say: Stimulant intoxication produces euphoria with mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension and dangerous hyperthermia. Severe toxicity causes chest pain, arrhythmia, seizures and muscle breakdown in patients. Benzodiazepines are first line treatment because they reduce agitation and cardiovascular stress. Contingency management has strong evidence because no approved substitution medicine exists currently.

steps.tx: **Nicotine dependence** drives preventable death mainly through smoking related cardiovascular and respiratory diseases in adults. Brief advice combined with pharmacotherapy greatly improves quit success compared with unaided attempts by smokers. Combination treatment uses a **nicotine patch** plus a short acting form for breakthrough craving during the day. **Varenicline** gives high quit rates through partial agonism and remains an important single agent option. Adults may quit through complete switching while young never smokers should never start nicotine.
steps.say: Nicotine dependence drives preventable death mainly through smoking related diseases in adults. Brief advice combined with pharmacotherapy greatly improves quit success for motivated smokers. Combination treatment uses a nicotine patch plus short acting forms for craving. Varenicline gives high quit rates and remains an important single agent option.

steps.tx: Many other substances cause distinctive harm patterns that examiners test through focused clinical vignettes regularly. MDMA can cause **serotonin toxicity** and dilutional hyponatraemia when users drink excessive water. Inhalants can cause sudden death from arrhythmia and lasting cognitive damage after repeated use. **GHB withdrawal** can become severe and needs high dose benzodiazepine treatment under close supervision. Ketamine causes ulcerative cystitis and dependence while synthetic cannabinoids cause severe agitation and psychosis. **Polysubstance use** is common and clinicians must inventory prescribed, recreational and online drugs.
steps.say: MDMA can cause serotonin toxicity and dangerous hyponatraemia in recreational users. Inhalants can cause sudden arrhythmia and lasting cognitive damage after repeated use. GHB withdrawal can become severe and needs closely supervised benzodiazepine treatment. Ketamine damages the bladder and synthetic cannabinoids cause severe psychosis in users.
